text: At the 1904 Olympics, the marathon winner was given rat poison.
And that wasn't even the strangest part.
The race was in Saint Louis, in ninety-degree heat, on dusty dirt roads.
Cars drove ahead of the runners, kicking up huge clouds of dust.
And there were only two places to get water on the entire course.
The first man across the finish line was Fred Lorz.
The crowd cheered.
Then they found out he'd ridden ten miles of it in a car.
One runner from Cuba stopped to eat apples from an orchard.
They were rotten.
So he lay down and took a nap.
He still finished fourth.
Another runner was chased a mile off course by dogs.
And the real winner, Thomas Hicks, was barely alive.
His trainers kept him going with egg whites, brandy, and strychnine.
Luckily, he made it to the finish line.
Unluckily, his trainers had to carry him across it.
Out of thirty-two runners, only fourteen finished.
And the man who rode in the car? The next year, he won the Boston Marathon.
On foot.
